canonical_claim: Provisional intended theorem family: if X is a closed, oriented, smooth, simply connected four-manifold whose integral intersection form is definite, then that form is diagonalizable over the integers; after choosing the positive-definite orientation it is equivalent to the standard positive diagonal form.
domain_and_universes: A closed oriented smooth simply connected four-manifold X, its integral second homology modulo torsion, and the induced unimodular symmetric intersection pairing; exact Lean universes and object model are open.
ordered_binders: smooth closed oriented four-manifold structure on X
hypotheses: X is smooth, closed, oriented, and four-dimensional
the integral intersection form is positive definite, or definite with orientation reversal handled explicitly
conclusion: The integral intersection lattice is integrally equivalent to a diagonal lattice (the identity matrix in the positive-definite orientation).
degenerate_and_boundary_cases: torsion in second homology and the quotient used to define the lattice
unresolved_scope_choices: exact theorem and page in an immutable primary-source copy
whether the selected root is stated only for positive-definite forms or symmetrically for definite forms
the source's compact/closed and boundary conventions
the precise carrier and equivalence relation for the integral intersection form
treatment of rank zero and orientation reversal
